headline: Highest risk is TREK’s default access to sensitive travel data and secrets; pairwise interaction with awesome-python is otherwise low because the first profile is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-python is a non-runnable collection with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest TREK output. TREK can use MCP and browsers, but there is no documented shared channel between the pair. The only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or external reuse of content, which keeps the injection pathway unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies TREK-generated text into a downstream parser that trusts it as instructions.
IF a shared MCP or filesystem bridge is added between the two agents.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted model output into automation.
Add a human review step before any instruction-like text is reused.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared content channel.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-python touches no data classes and has no I/O surfaces, while TREK handles sensitive items like API keys, MFA secrets, and reservations. There is no shared workspace or authenticated channel documented here, so leakage from the pair is not default. The main risk is accidental exposure if TREK outputs sensitive context into a place the other agent can read.
conditions: IF TREK writes secrets or reservation data into a shared file that awesome-python can read.
IF an operator exports TREK logs or documents into a common workspace.
mitigations: Store TREK secrets outside shared folders.
Rotate any exposed API keys or MFA secrets immediately.
Restrict file permissions on ./data and ./uploads.
Review logs for accidental secret emission.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents into separate OS users or containers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python has no write, network, or concurrency surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. TREK does support real-time collaborative sessions and multiple instances, but without a second writable agent there is no overlapping write set or lock conflict in this pair. The pathway is therefore blocked by agent A’s lack of mutation capability.
conditions: IF awesome-python is replaced with a runnable agent that can write the same files or mutate the same OAuth scopes as TREK.
mitigations: Keep awesome-python as a read-only reference source.
Avoid giving both agents write access to the same directory.
Use per-agent credentials for any shared service.
requires-engineering: add locking around TREK’s mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-python is a static repository, not an action-taking agent, so TREK cannot reliably treat its output as authoritative operational input by default. TREK does have AI built in and can act on travel workflows, but the pair lacks a documented pipeline where A’s output is automatically consumed by B. That makes cascading error possible only through manual reuse.
conditions: IF an operator pastes awesome-python content into TREK as if it were validated travel guidance or code.
IF TREK is configured to auto-ingest external text without verification.
mitigations: Require source verification before TREK acts on imported text.
Do not feed repository listings directly into travel decisions.
Add a confirmation prompt before any downstream action.
requires-engineering: implement citation/provenance checks in TREK.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles sensitive personal and account data, including email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while awesome-python is an open-source repository with no data classes touched. The pair itself does not show a residency mismatch, but TREK’s handling of secrets and logs creates a compliance burden if those artifacts are exposed or retained improperly. The other agent is not cited for residency because it has no relevant data flow.
conditions: IF TREK stores secrets or personal data in ./data/logs/trek.log beyond the intended retention period.
IF TREK processes EU personal data without a documented DPA or residency control.
mitigations: Review TREK retention settings for logs and uploads.
Delete any unnecessary stored secrets or confirmation numbers.
Confirm a DPA and residency policy for personal data.
Limit access to ./data/logs/trek.log.
requires-engineering: add configurable retention and deletion workflows.
